coverage_note: State, local government, school district and University of Minnesota employees under the Public Employment Labor Relations Act (PELRA), Minn. Stat. 179A.01 to 179A.25. Representation and mediation run through the Bureau of Mediation Services commissioner; unfair labor practice charges go to the Public Employment Relations Board.

governing_statute.value: Public Employment Labor Relations Act (PELRA), Minn. Stat. 179A.01 to 179A.25
governing_statute.quote: It is the public policy of this state and the purpose of sections 179A.01 to 179A.25 to promote orderly and constructive relationships between all public employers and their employees.

impasse_procedure.value: Mediation by the Bureau of Mediation Services. Essential employees (police, firefighters, and other listed groups) may petition for binding interest arbitration; for other employees, interest arbitration requires mutual agreement, and they may strike after the statutory conditions are met.
impasse_procedure.quote: An exclusive representative or employer of a unit of essential employees may petition for binding interest arbitration by filing a written request with the other party and the commissioner.

agency_fee_status.value: Not collectible. PELRA still contains a fair share fee provision, but Janus v. AFSCME (2018) bars agency fees from nonconsenting public employees, so it cannot be enforced.
agency_fee_status.quote: (a) An exclusive representative may require employees who are not members of the exclusive representative to contribute a fair share fee for services rendered by the exclusive representative.
